Match.id is a dense sequential key 1–25979 and a match is not a country; the 11 sparse country ids fall inside that range purely by chance (coverage 0).
Player_Attributes.id is a dense sequential key 1–183978 for player-attribute rows, unrelated to countries; the overlap is incidental (coverage 0).

League.country_id values exactly match Country.id with full containment and coverage, and sample rows align semantically (England Premier League → England, Germany Bundesliga → Germany), so this is the real reference.

League.id and Country.id share the exact same 11 values and sample rows show league id 1729/7809/17642 matching countries England/Germany/Portugal, indicating League reuses the Country key pool (league is a one-to-one extension keyed by country).
Match.id is a sequential 1..25979 primary key for match rows, and a league cannot be a kind of match, so the full containment of the 11 league ids is coincidental small-integer overlap.
Player_Attributes.id is a sequential 1..183978 row key for player rating snapshots, and a league is not a player attribute row, so the overlap is coincidental.

The source is a FIFA team identifier while the target is a surrogate row id for player-attribute snapshots; the full containment with 0.2% coverage is just small-integer overlap between unrelated ID spaces, and a team cannot reference a player-attribute row.
A league's country_id cannot reference a Match primary key; the overlap is coincidental because both use small sequential integer IDs from unrelated ranges.
A league's country_id cannot reference a Player_Attributes primary key; the overlap is coincidental small-integer ID collision with no semantic relationship.

Match.id is a sequential surrogate key for match rows, and a team_api_id value cannot identify a match; the overlap is coincidental because team ids fall inside the 1..25979 range.
Player.id is a sequential surrogate key for players, and a team is not a player, so the ~98% containment is chance overlap of small integers rather than a real reference.
